title: Day 663: Morena Senator Enrique Inzunza Cazárez Surrenders to US Federal Authorities in San Diego — Third of Ten SDNY-Indicted Officials in US Custody
detail: On Day 663 of the Sinaloa cartel civil war — May 17, 2026 — Enrique Inzunza Cazárez, 53, a sitting Morena senator from Sinaloa and former Secretary General of the Sinaloa state government under Governor Rubén Rocha Moya, surrendered to US federal authorities in San Diego, California, becoming the third of the ten Mexican officials indicted by the Southern District of New York on April 29, 2026 to face US justice. Inzunza Cazárez is a uniquely critical figure in the SDNY indictment package: the 34-page superseding indictment alleges he served as the direct operational intermediary between Los Chapitos — specifically Iván Archivaldo Guzmán Salazar — and Governor Rocha Moya. Before the 2021 Sinaloa gubernatorial election, he allegedly met with Iván Archivaldo and provided the Guzmán brothers with the names and home addresses of Rocha Moya's political opponents so Chapitos operatives could run targeted intimidation campaigns to eliminate electoral rivals. After Rocha Moya won the election, Inzunza allegedly embedded 'corrupt officials' throughout the Sinaloa state government architecture to protect Chapitos drug operations from law enforcement interference. He faces narcotics importation conspiracy and weapons conspiracy charges — including conspiracy to possess machine guns and destructive devices — carrying a maximum sentence of life in prison. Inzunza Cazárez was elected to the Mexican Senate in August 2024, giving him active legislative immunity (fuero constitucional) under Mexican law. His voluntary surrender in San Diego bypassed both Mexican sovereign extradition proceedings and the senatorial immunity protection — an extraordinary break from legal convention that dramatically escalates pressure on the seven remaining indicted officials still in Mexico, including Rocha Moya. Former Mexican President Felipe Calderón publicly commented on the surrenders of Sinaloa officials on May 17. Running toll: ~2,425+ homicides since September 9, 2024; El Mayo EDNY sentencing July 20, 2026.
